claim: The 2026-07-10 raw-body and terminal-tombstone CAS plan was superseded and rejected because it recreated the rejected generation-in-key design; the replacement named by the plan is `2026-07-10-cas-freshness-meta-v3.md`.

The rejected raw-body plan defined a per-hash `.meta` descriptor as a three-state `{clean, condemned, tombstone}` register whose etag is the sole linearization token, while blob bodies are raw immutable content and the writer-side `RetireView`, syncer, `observed_gc_round`, and ack-floor are removed.

In the raw-body design, a blob body is stored at `blobs/xx/<hash>` as a raw payload written once with `PUT If-None-Match`, while its meta is stored at `blobs/xx/<hash>.meta` and is the only conditionally-operated object.
The invariant `INV-META-BODY` requires a present meta to imply a present body; it is maintained by creating bottom-up (body then meta) and deleting top-down (meta then body).
The writer's deduplication path uses one point-read of the meta under strong read-after-write consistency, and GC changes condemn, spare, and delete state by CASing the meta.
GC deletion in the raw-body design is a tombstone handshake: transition meta from `condemned` to `tombstone`, delete the body, then delete the tombstone meta, using a bounded parallel pool.

A `tombstone` meta is terminal: a writer must never CAS `tombstone` to `clean`, because GC may already have committed deletion of the unchanged-token body; the writer instead waits boundedly for the meta to become absent and then fresh-uploads, failing with `ABORTED` on exhaustion.
Birth-completion is allowed only from an absent meta, representing a crashed pre-meta birth; it is never allowed from a `tombstone` meta.
Every meta write carries a fresh `incarnation` `UInt128` nonce because content-derived S3 etags would otherwise allow a clean-meta ABA; the nonce makes each meta encoding and etag unique.
A GC delete may delete a body only after winning the `condemned` to `tombstone` CAS; the terminal tombstone prevents a writer from re-establishing the body after that claim.

CAS is pre-release in this plan, so adding metas and removing the blob envelope requires recreating existing development pools; no migration, dual read/write path, or compatibility configuration is retained.
The destructive path fails closed: GC never deletes a body without a won tombstone claim, while a 404 during fold is recorded and continued rather than throwing or fail-closing the fold.

A condemned object is never read or fetched to revive it; revival uses a fresh upload or recreation from source, except for the documented `INV-1` tokenless copy-forward of a committed-source dependency whose condemned body is still present.
The one-GET meta-adopt path requires a backend with strong read-after-write consistency; the plan identifies S3 since 2020 and RustFS as satisfying that requirement.
GC condemn, spare, and delete meta operations must use a bounded parallel pool because one million sequential operations at approximately 20 ms each would take about 5.5 hours per pass.

The TLA+ model `CaMetaDescriptorRaw.tla` is the authority for the writer-GC state machine, whose required transitions are `FreshUpload`, `Adopt`, `Resurrect`, `BirthCompletion`, `GcCondemn`, `GcSpare`, and `GcDeletePhaseA/B/C`.

The committed-removal sweep must preserve a body after a `-1` removal is appended but before that removal is sealed by the GC fold, because the fold still needs the body to emit the decrement; the body becomes sweepable only after the removal is sealed.

The meta codec uses magic `CAMT`, version 2, state, `condemn_round`, size, and a 16-byte `incarnation` field; decoding rejects bad magic, unsupported version, invalid state, wrong length, and the old pre-incarnation length with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
`Layout::blobMetaKey` returns `blobKey(id) + ".meta"`.

The shared meta-ops API consists of `loadMeta`, `putMetaIfAbsent`, `casMeta`, and `deleteMetaExact`; `loadMeta` returns an optional `LoadedMeta` containing the decoded `BlobMeta` and etag, and an absent meta returns `nullopt`.

`ca-fsck` reports `meta_without_body` for a meta with no body as an `INV-META-BODY` violation, reports `body_without_meta` for a body with no meta as benign pre-meta-birth debris, and `clean()` requires both `dangling == 0` and `meta_without_body == 0`.
Under raw bodies, `ca-inspect` dispatches `.meta` keys to `BlobMeta` decoding and renders non-meta `blobs/` keys as raw blobs with size and a hash-match check rather than decoding an envelope.

`putBlob` writes the raw body with `casPut` and then creates clean meta with `putMetaIfAbsent`; a body precondition conflict or meta creation conflict enters the meta observation path, and dependency tokens store the meta etag rather than the body token.

The writer's meta state machine adopts a clean meta without a body `HEAD`, resurrects a condemned meta with `casMeta` and no body re-upload, and handles an absent meta by re-establishing the raw body from its own source before creating clean meta.

A writer observing a tombstone waits through bounded fresh meta reads and then retries fresh upload after the meta becomes absent; if the bound is exhausted, `putBlob` throws `ABORTED` and never changes the tombstone to clean.
Raw blob reads resolve at offset 0, and new-pool `blob_header_len` is set to 0 and retained only as a legacy pool-meta field.
Promote skips meta revalidation for tokened leaves; for a non-tokened leaf it fails with `ABORTED` on absent meta, accepts clean meta, and copy-forwards only a condemned meta by CASing it to clean.
`copyForwardFromCondemned` is a pure meta CAS for a condemned raw-body leaf and performs no body GET or PUT; tombstone or absent meta is fail-closed because the tokenless promote path has no source.

GC condemns a clean meta by CASing it to condemned and stores the resulting condemned-meta etag in `RetiredEntry.token`; it spares by CASing condemned to clean and ignores absent or tombstone metas during the condemn pass.
Graduation is determined by `condemn_round < current_round`, where `current_round` is `new_round = state.round + 1`; using `state.round` would prevent entries from graduating.

GC supersede detection re-reads meta for net-zero-touched entries and compares the current meta etag with the stored condemned-meta etag; a mismatch means the retired entry refers to a newer incarnation.

The GC rebuild skips `.meta` keys in the `blobs/` listing, captures or repairs the corresponding meta for each body, and stores the condemned-meta etag rather than the body token in rebuilt retired state.

The writer-side `RetireView`, its syncer, `observed_gc_round`, and ack-floor are removed; `MountLease` loses `observed_gc_round`, the beat publishes only `{now, min_active}`, and GC round recovery no longer uses `min_ack` or `max_ack`.
The deterministic GC-delete-versus-writer race must prove that after GC wins `condemned` to `tombstone`, a writer observes the tombstone and fails with `ABORTED` instead of un-tombstoning it.

The 2026-07-10 CAS ref-log handoff design is obsolete and was superseded by `2026-07-11-cas-ref-table-snapshot-log-design.md` rev.5, which landed as Phase 1; rev.6 is a lease-boundary exclusivity proposal.

In the obsolete ref-log design, `cas/refs` is only an append-only inbox from the mounted writer to GC, and authoritative namespace state is the adopted GC ref fold plus the contiguous writer-log tail.

The obsolete ref handoff transfers a contiguous writer-log prefix into the GC generation through the existing single `gc/state` CAS; before that CAS the prefix is authoritative, and after it the GC fold is authoritative.
After a successful ref-fold adoption, consumed `_log` objects may be deleted in bounded batches; an interrupted post-CAS deletion leaves only physical debris and is not a second protocol phase.

The writer records an exact precommit removal before retiring a failed build, while a newly mounted writer fences the predecessor epoch and appends one constant-size epoch clear per affected namespace.

`dropNamespace` is represented as one constant-size `remove_namespace` transaction that atomically clears committed and precommit bindings and changes the incarnation to `Removed`; it does not serialize the owner list.
Phase 1 of the obsolete ref-log design rewrites one complete folded ref base for each productive handoff, while idle and deferred rounds carry the exact parent base without reading or rewriting it.

The obsolete design reserved Phase 2 for measured optimizations such as delta `RunFile` levels, leveled compaction, Bloom or fence-pointer metadata, adaptive handoff thresholds, and optional preflight or per-namespace restart; no Phase 1 authority or invariant may depend on them.
A writer-log object can be removed only when the adopted fold seal names a valid `RefBaseSet` whose namespace row has the same incarnation and `folded_seq >= log_record.seq`.
Replay starts at `folded_seq + 1`, or at sequence one for an empty base; a gap before the maximum observed sequence is an exception that disables destructive actions for that namespace.
Every writer-log key and GC ref-fold entry contains the namespace incarnation, so an older incarnation cannot cover or consume a newer incarnation's sequence numbers.
A writer does not retire a build while it owns a precommit; if the process stops first, only a successor that fenced the entire predecessor epoch may append the namespace-scoped epoch clear.
`remove_namespace` changes `Live` to `Removed` and clears every owner binding in one replay transition; no later mutation is valid for that incarnation.
Orphan cleanup protects current owners and every manifest removed in the unadopted tail using the exact adopted `RefBaseSet` plus the complete validated writer tail.

A warm-cache isolated ref mutation creates one `_log` object and performs zero ref-state reads, while a compatible batch of `B` mutations shares one `putIfAbsent`; uncertain writes are resolved by an exact-key `GET`.

The required read-after-write visibility contract applies to both ref-log `LIST` and canonical ordering: a backend without visibility or ordering cannot enable the format and may not substitute an unbounded in-memory sort.
Every reachability effect in a candidate ref base is resolved before the fold seal, destructive GC action, and generation `CAS`; any required manifest-body failure aborts the whole attempt.

`WriterId` is `{ writer_epoch, writer_sequence }`, both components are nonzero `UInt64` values, each successful mount strictly increases `writer_epoch`, and `writer_sequence` starts at one within an epoch.
`WriterId` renders as two fixed-width 16-digit lower-case hexadecimal components, for example `0000000000000007-000000000000008e`; upper-case, shortened, zero, and overflowing forms are rejected.
The same `WriterId` identifies build ownership, the prefix of each `ManifestRef`, and a namespace incarnation; `birth_gc_round` remains separate and orders a new namespace incarnation relative to GC.
`ManifestRef` is `{writer_id, manifest_ordinal}` with ordinal range 1 through 999999, and canonical manifest paths include `cas/manifests/<namespace>/<writer_id>/<000001>.proto`.
All archive namespaces end in `@cas@`, and `shadowNamespace` must preserve that suffix.
Ref-log objects use `cas/refs/<archive-ns@cas@>/_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/...`, where `seq` is a fixed-width 16-digit lower-case hexadecimal sequence beginning at one.

Inline ref-log records use `_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/precommit/<manifest_ref_suffix>/<ref...>`, `_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/abandon/<manifest_ref_suffix>/<ref...>`, `_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/drop/<manifest_ref_suffix>/<ref...>`, `_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/clear-precommits-before/<writer_epoch>`, or `_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/remove-namespace`.
Body-bearing ref-log records use `_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/tx/<body_hash>.proto`, where `body_hash` is the lower-case 32-digit hexadecimal `CityHash128` of the deterministic stored bytes.

A `RefLogTxn` contains `header`, `namespace`, `namespace_incarnation`, `seq`, and repeated `RefOp ops`; supported operations are `namespace_birth`, `owner_transition`, `set_payload`, `clear_precommits_before`, and `remove_namespace`.

A transaction containing `namespace_birth` and its optional first owner transition runs alone; `clear_precommits_before` and `remove_namespace` also run alone, and a batch never crosses its encoded-size or operation-count limit.

`namespace_birth` is operation zero of sequence one, creates `Live` state for the physical incarnation key, normally includes the first precommit add, and has `birth_gc_round` no greater than the current decoded `gc/state.round`.
A promote operation requires `Live` state, the exact old precommit, a committed binding naming the same `ManifestRef`, and a complete initial `RootRef` payload.
A current-build precommit removal requires the build to remain locally active until the exact removal record is durable; the replay transition is not liveness-dependent.
A committed ref removal requires the exact committed binding and removes its `RootRef` payload.
A payload update requires a live committed ref still naming `expected_manifest_ref`; it replaces the complete mutable payload and changes no reachability edge.

Applying `remove_namespace` clears committed refs, precommits, and payloads, changes state to `Removed`, and makes a second durable remove record corruption; API idempotency returns success after observing `Removed`.

Writable startup fences the predecessor, verifies the exact adopted fold seal, installs its `RefBaseSet` metadata, and lazily loads each namespace by reading its base rows and replaying its complete tail between before/after `gc/state` checks.
The initial default for `ref_state_cache_bytes` is 256 MiB, and the obsolete Phase 1 design uses byte-bounded LRU caches for coherent namespace views and indexed run blocks.
A successful append leaves no dirty ref-state memory because the log is authoritative; complete namespace views may be evicted immediately, and eviction never writes storage.

The common write path validates under the namespace lock, writes one inline key or deterministic batch transaction with `putIfAbsent`, resolves an uncertain precondition failure by reading the same key, and applies the transition to memory only after the log is authoritative.

For a current-writer failure, the writer keeps the build active, appends the exact precommit removal, and retires the build only after that removal is durable; if the append fails, the build remains active and the error propagates.
A namespace recreation at the same archive path is allowed only after the old namespace-file prefix is empty, uses a strictly greater `NamespaceIncarnation`, and starts again at sequence one.

Phase 1 GC stores one complete canonical ref base under `gc/gen/<generation>/attempt/<attempt>/ref-base/<run_ordinal>.run`, and the fold seal names each exact `RunRef`, checksum, minimum key, and maximum key.

Ref-base row keys are `NamespaceMeta`, `Committed`, or `Precommit` tuples beginning with `LogPrefix(ns) = canonical_namespace_bytes(ns) || "/_log/"`; memcomparable encoding preserves canonical object-key `LIST` order, including prefix-related namespaces.
The initial target size for a ref-base run is `Q = 8 MiB`, and ref-base PUTs satisfy `ref_base_puts <= ceil(S_next / Q) + 1` for `S_next` bytes in the complete next base.
A point ref lookup selects at most one base run using non-overlapping key bounds; a cold run normally requires `HEAD`, a footer range `GET`, and an indexed-block range `GET`.

GC processes namespaces in canonical tuple-key order, selects at most one complete transaction prefix per namespace per generation, and never returns to a namespace after emitting its output; any suffix remains in `_log` for a later generation.

A live owner newly entering the fold requires a valid manifest body, an inherited-owner removal requires that body to emit `-1`, a move preserving the same `ManifestRef` emits no delta, and a missing required manifest aborts the entire GC attempt.

If a late manifest-body failure occurs after tentative output runs or reachability artifacts are finalized, those artifacts remain unadopted; the fold seal is not written, `gc/state` is not changed, and no destructive GC or writer-log deletion occurs.

A productive ref handoff is forced by fold-delta threshold, ref-tail pressure, maximum defer age, destructive demand, or `remove_namespace`; a deferred round still replays the complete tail for destructive protection.
After a successful `gc/state` CAS, GC deletes covered ref-log objects with exact-key batch deletes of at most 1000 keys per request; if the CAS loses, it deletes no ref-log object.

The orphan-manifest sweep proves build retirement, reads the exact adopted `RefBaseSet`, replays the complete contiguous tail, rechecks `gc/state`, and deletes only candidates absent from the complete protection set.

For one productive ref handoff, the obsolete design models writer cost as `K` PUTs, GC log intake as `A·K` body reads plus `ceil(K/1000)` LIST pages, productive ref-fold reads as `3R + H`, and post-adoption trim as `ceil(K/1000)` DELETE requests.

For a 1 MiB run block and a 16 MiB `gc_ref_fold_namespace_bytes` budget, the obsolete Phase 1 ref-fold construction requires about 17 MiB plus small bounded buffers, independent of total live-ref cardinality.

The failure table requires a lost GC generation CAS to leave the attempt unadopted and delete no logs, while a stop after a successful CAS treats the new fold as authoritative and repeats covered-log deletion later.

If `gc/state` is lost, attempt-local ref-base runs are not independently authoritative; offline rebuild may conservatively union surviving runs and logs, may over-protect storage, and returns writable authority only after an explicit recovery action adopts a new baseline.

The obsolete ref-log design explicitly rejects a mutable `_head`, a `_snap` service area, a second ref adoption CAS, GC-generated writer records, cross-namespace atomic rename, and compatibility with unreleased `RootShardManifest` or decimal manifest-key layouts.

The retired-in-snapshot plan makes each per-shard source-edge run carry condemned state at the existing zero-sentinel key, adds a per-shard `CondemnedSummary` to the fold seal, and removes `RetiredSet`, `CART`, `retiredKey`, and `GcState::retired_refs`.

Settlement semantics remain byte-for-byte unchanged in the retired-in-snapshot plan: condemn, carry, graduate with `delete_pending`, redelete, clamp suppression, pre-CAS single delete site, resurrect-supersede, `.meta` writes, B170 events, and GC-log counters are preserved.
A carried condemned sentinel is settlement-only: it never sets the merge touch bit, emits no zero marker, and does not trigger `peek_head` when carry is the only activity.

Source-edge run readers fail closed on `key_schema != 1`, wrong run kind, unknown `token_type`, truncated payload, an edge row at `source_id = 0`, a sentinel row at nonzero `source_id`, unknown row type, or duplicate sentinel; missing adopted seal or missing `condemned_summary` at `snap_generation > 0` makes `graduationDue` return true.
The source-edge run format defines `kEdgeActive = 0x01`, `kZeroMarker = 0x00`, `kCondemned = 0x02`, and `kSourceEdgeKeySchema = 1`; old source-edge runs with `key_schema = 0` fail closed.
A `CondemnedRow` stores `delete_pending`, the full `Token`, `size`, and `condemn_round`; `encodeCondemnedRow` uses `[0x02][flags][token_type][round][size][len][value]`.
`openSourceEdgeRun` validates `RunKind::SourceEdge` and `key_schema == kSourceEdgeKeySchema`, and `assertValidSourceEdgeId` reserves `UInt128{0}` for the condemned sentinel namespace.

The 2-cursor settlement merge removes the separate `prior_retired` input: condemned rows are decoded from the prior source-edge run, settled at blob close-out, and emitted back at the blob's zero-sentinel key.
Fresh condemns emit `kCondemned` rows, absent-at-condemn cases emit `kZeroMarker` as before, prior zero markers are dropped on carry, and carried condemned rows do not set `cur_touched`.
With `suppress_destructive`, pending rows carry unchanged and floor-passed rows remain condemned-only, preserving the row bytes.
Every new fold seal contains a `condemned_summary` total over shards `0..gc_shards-1`; folding computes it from written condemned rows, while pure-carry shards copy the parent's entry verbatim.

`CondemnedSummary` contains `condemned_total`, `pending_total`, and `oldest_nonpending_condemn_round`, with `UINT64_MAX` meaning no nonpending condemned row; the protobuf field is `repeated CondemnedSummaryProto condemned_summary = 7`.

For `snap_generation == 0`, `graduationDue` returns false; otherwise it reads the adopted seal and fails closed by returning true when the seal is missing, undecodable, or its summary is not total over `gc_shards`.

When the adopted seal summary is valid, `graduationDue` is true exactly when some shard has `pending_total > 0` or `oldest_nonpending_condemn_round < current_round`; it requires no backend GET beyond the seal read.

`previewDeletes` emits a `PreviewEntry` for every `kCondemned` row using the stored token, size, and condemn round; `delete_pending` maps to `reason = "delete_pending"`, otherwise to `reason = "awaiting_graduation"`, and these rows require no `HEAD`.
The existing zero-marker plus `HEAD` path remains the source of `PreviewEntry` records with `reason = "unreachable"`; the condemned-row output is a superset of the previous preview output.
`fsck` collects condemned rows during the same streaming pass over seal-named source-edge runs that it uses for reachability, replacing the `retired_refs` loop.
`ca-inspect` reports per-shard `condemned_summary` fields named `condemned_total`, `pending_total`, and `oldest_nonpending_condemn_round` instead of dumping the `retired_refs` map.

GC rebuild must first traverse journals and accumulate per-shard deltas and `edge_bearing`, then list physical blobs and head zero-edge bodies, mint condemned rows, append them to shard runs, seal summaries, and only then CAS `gc/state`.
The rebuilt orphan rows use `CondemnedRow{token, size, condemn_round = minted_round}` and graduate when `condemn_round < current_round`, which is the next round after minting.
The retired-in-snapshot plan requires `05008_ca_gc_snap_prune` to remain unmodified because it is the settlement-semantics oracle for the refactor.

A writer mutation exists exactly when a durable operation exists in its `_log` object; one `_log` object may contain a bounded flat-combined batch, and its key plus body are the complete operation encoding.
Only the mounted writer allocates namespace log sequence numbers; GC never appends to the writer log.
Every owner add, move, payload update, removal, and namespace removal is a writer-log operation; GC only replays those operations.
The existing GC generation CAS co-adopts reachability runs, the fold seal, and the exact `RefBaseSet`; there is no independent ref adoption state.

The fold seal is the exact recovery base: it names every authoritative base `RunRef`, its checksum, and non-overlapping row-key bounds, and consumers never select a run merely because `LIST` found it.
A writer-log key conflict is an exception and must not be bypassed by skipping to a later sequence.
An append that exceeds the namespace tail or decoded-row bound fails before object creation and retains the current sequence.

A corrupt adopted fold seal or ref run causes writable startup and destructive maintenance to fail closed; an unknown future format version produces the repository's future-format exception rather than falling back to an older format.

The raw-body writer retains the large-body head-first guard so a large likely dedup hit does not stream a body merely to receive a precondition failure, addressing the `B168` P2 and `B187` broken-pipe concerns.
`CaB140DangleMerge.tla` remains the minimal historical counterexample for trimming before adoption and is not changed by the retired-in-snapshot refactor.

The retired-in-snapshot validation requires the S30 resurrect-churn/recurring-hash scenario and the S33 concurrent-leader scenario to pass; S33 guards the concurrent-leader reclaim-leak regression and S30 covers the resurrect-supersede path.
